top_signals.title: Gold Pushes Higher as Weaker Dollar Offsets Inflation Risks
top_signals.summary: Gold pushed higher — after a three-day decline — as a weakening dollar offset inflation concerns stemming from renewed attacks on ships in the Middle East.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Diesel Crunch Threatens Lasting Price Pain, Consumption Cutbacks
top_signals.summary: The global refining sector’s diesel crunch is likely to result in tight supply for the coming months, keeping prices high and weighing on demand, according to analysts and traders.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Commodity repricing impacting inflation expectations and industrial supply chains.

top_signals.title: Waterborne shipments from the U.S. Gulf Coast increased in April and May
top_signals.summary: Waterborne shipments of crude oil and petroleum products from the U.S. Gulf Coast (PADD 3) to the West Coast (PADD 5) more than quadrupled year-on-year in April and May following a waiver that permitted a broader group of ships to travel between U.S. ports. Shipments from the U.S. Gulf Coast to the East Coast (PADD 1) also increased.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Commodity repricing impacting inflation expectations and industrial supply chains.

top_signals.title: Ex-BOK Governor Rhee on Won Volatility
top_signals.summary: Former Bank of Korea Governor Rhee Chang Yong says South Koreans needn’t worry too much about short-term volatility in the won. He speaks with Bloomberg's Stephen Engle in a wide-ranging fireside chat at the KB Financial Group Korea Conference in Seoul. (Source: Bloomberg)
